Environmental Biology, PhD
Lead the Research. Shape the Field. Advance Biodiversity Science.
At the doctoral level, you’re not just studying environmental biology — you’re expanding it.
The Ph.D. in Environmental Biology is designed for researchers ready to make original
contributions to the field. Whether entering with a bachelor’s or building on a master’s
degree, doctoral students develop and lead independent research that advances understanding
of biodiversity, ecosystems and environmental change.
Your work won’t just live in a classroom or lab. It will contribute to the scientific
community — often forming the foundation for publications, future research and long-term
impact in academia, policy or applied science.
Immersive and Self-Directed
You’ll design and execute original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor,
contributing new knowledge to your area of expertise.
Along the way, you’ll build advanced skills in:
Research design and methodology
Scientific writing and publication
Data analysis and interpretation
Grant-supported research collaboration
Teaching and mentoring at the undergraduate level
The program culminates in a dissertation (or equivalent peer-reviewed publications),
supported by both written and oral candidacy examinations and a formal defense.
With flexible entry points and individualized study plans, your Ph.D. experience is
shaped by your research goals — and the questions you’re driven to answer.
Research That Contributes to the Field
This isn’t guided coursework with a research component — it’s research at the center.
Doctoral students work closely with faculty whose projects are actively shaping environmental
science, often supported by external research funding. Your work becomes part of larger
scientific conversations, with opportunities to publish, present and contribute to
meaningful advancements in biodiversity and conservation science.
A Focused Environment for Serious Environmental Research
At ESF, your research exists within a community fully dedicated to environmental science.
That focus means access to faculty expertise, field sites, research infrastructure
and collaborators who are deeply engaged in ecological and conservation work. It also
means your research is surrounded by peers equally committed to advancing environmental
knowledge.
Add in opportunities to teach, mentor and develop professionally, and the result is
a doctoral experience that prepares you for leadership in both academic and applied
settings.
On Campus
Fall or Spring Start

Outcomes and Career Opportunities
Ph.D. graduates move into roles that shape research, policy and practice. Whether
pursuing academia or applied science, graduates leave prepared to lead complex research
initiatives, secure funding and influence environmental decision-making at high levels.
Career paths include
University and College Faculty
Research Scientists
Policy Advisors and Analysts
Senior Scientists in Government and NGOs
Environmental Research Leaders in Industry
Current Student Resources
Doctoral students complete a minimum of 60 credits, including advanced coursework,
seminars and dissertation research. Progression to candidacy requires successful completion
of written and oral examinations, followed by a dissertation defense.
